title: Coordinated epochal shift for active-active gateway with streaming-aware load-shedding and circuit breakers
creator: Aisha Park
description: Background: We operate an active-active hosted API across multiple regions. Recent incident post-massive-deploy showed degraded streaming session availability during a controlled regional capacity reclaim. Current failover behavior bluntly shifts traffic which causes long-lived streaming sessions to disconnect and creates KV cache miss storms and tail-latency spikes.
goals: Design a coordinated multi-region failover procedure that minimizes stream disconnects and preserves SLOs (p50/p95 latency, availability)
Implement an "epochal" handoff token and a short-lived routing epoch to gracefully steer new connections and finish in-flight streams
Integrate per-route circuit breakers and soft load-shedding so tail-latency and error budgets are respected during region transitions
Provide roll-forward observability (per-epoch telemetry) and safety knobs for ops (abort/rollback, emergency hard-cut)
success_criteria: <1% streaming-session disconnects attributable to failover during canary experiments
No >2x increase in 95th percentile token-latency across affected routes
Operational runbook with automated rollback and a single CLI command to abort an epochal shift
Dashboards that show per-epoch traffic distribution, cache hit ratio, and shed-rate
design_summary: Introduce an epoch token appended to the client routing header (X-Rdl-Epoch) that encodes: region-origin, epoch-id (monotonic), and an expiry TTL. Gateways accept the token and use epoch semantics: during a shift we enter a two-phase epoch transition: (1) soft-ramp: new connections are weighted away from target region while incumbent region drains in-flight streams; (2) hard-finish: after grace TTL, remaining sessions are either migrated (if client supports resume token) or politely terminated. Migration uses a resume token with sequence offsets and minimal KV checkpoint transfer. Circuit breakers are attached to per-region queues using combined signals: queue depth, 95th latency, and supra-error-rate; threshold crossing triggers soft-shed strategy (priority-weighted token bucket) before hard-drop. Load-shedding policy supports tenant QoS tiers and route-level weights. All handoffs are coordinated by the control plane leader with a conservative inter-region ramp of <10% steps every 10s by default.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Longer drain TTL reduces disconnects but increases cross-region resource usage and cost
Resume-based migration requires client SDK changes — until adoption falls back to resume-unavailable path which increases disconnects
Adaptive ramp aggressiveness needs tuned heuristics; overly reactive ramp may oscillate between regions (risk mitigated by hysteresis/epoch monotonicity)
KV cache reconciliation introduces transient inconsistency — we rely on eventual consistency plus short-lived prefix cache to mask misses
implementation_plan: Phase 0: RFC + proto (this ticket) — define epoch header, resume token format, and control-plane APIs
Phase 1: Gateway runtime changes — accept/validate epochs, drain flow-control, per-route circuit-breaker hooks
Phase 2: Control plane coordination — epoch orchestration, leader election safe-guards, telemetry rollup per-epoch
Phase 3: SDK opt-in migration path for resume tokens and reconnection guidance
Phase 4: Canary in staging + cross-region chaos tests + progressive rollout to production
progress_updates: 2026-02-27: Spike: simulated epoched ramp in staging reproduces 40% fewer disconnects vs blunt shift; experiment artifacts: drive.google.com/filed/edge-epoch-sim (internal)
2026-03-02: Implemented epoch header parse in gateway dev branch; initial unit tests for TTL expiry and monotonic detection (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9876)
2026-03-07: Design review with platform and SDK teams — SDK agreed to opt-in resume token in next minor release; suggested change: encode resume offset as varint to reduce token size

2026-03-10: Observability plan sketched: per-epoch metric namespace (epoch.id, origin.region, target.region) and dashboards prototype at https://grafana.redwood.company/d/edge-epoch/overview (internal)

2026-03-13: Chaos run in staging (network partition + gateway drain): soft-ramp at 5% steps produced stable behavior; noted two issues — KV cache cold-start spike and a tenant with aggressive backoff that flooded the fallback path
open_questions: Should epoch tokens be publicly visible in logs? (PII/security concerns) — security prefers redaction for exported logs
What is the default epoch TTL for different route classes? (chat streaming vs embeddings) — proposal: 90s for streaming, 10s for short RPCs
Should we prefer migration over termination for premium tenants even if it requires temporarily hot-copying KV state?
review_feedback: Infra lead (Lina Chen): prefer a conservative default ramp (max 5%/10s) and require rate-limiter fallback on control-plane commands
SDK lead (Jon Patel): resume tokens OK but we need a minimal example and backwards compat strategy in the SDK changelog
SRE (Marcus Rey): add a kill-switch in Console (rollback epoch) and require a playbook step that verifies shard-reservation metrics before ramping beyond 25%
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch header parsing, TTL expiry, monotonic checks
Integration tests: resume-token roundtrip across gateways and sequence resumes for streams
Chaos tests: cross-region partition during soft-ramp and hard-finish; assert <=1% disconnects
Load tests: per-tenant weighted soft-shed under 2x normal QPS to validate queue depth triggers and shed-rate control
next_steps: Finish gateway runtime PR and add circuit-breaker knobs (in progress) — owner: Marco
Finalize SDK resume token spec and publish migration guide — owner: Jon Patel
Schedule staging canary with SRE and product observability — target window: 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-22
notes: This ticket focuses on reliability-first choreography for regional shifts. The separate ticket ENG-51821 will handle storage-layer snapshot optimization for migration hot-copying; keep cross-links updated.
